spec.title: Tailscale2OTel — Tailnet
spec.description: Tailnet observability: fleet and device hygiene, network flows (rollup + raw), security and audit, policy and configuration, node metrics, and Kubernetes audit. Sections appear only when their data is present in the target. Exporter health lives on the companion tailscale2otel-health dashboard. Generated by deploy/grafana/gen/build.py.

spec.title: Devices online / total / offline
spec.description: Devices currently reporting online, the total the exporter can see, and the remainder offline (normal for laptops and phones).

spec.title: Updates available
spec.description: Devices with a Tailscale client update waiting.

defaults.noValue: No device update data — needs the devices collector and a control plane that reports update availability.

spec.title: Users
spec.description: Users known to the tailnet, across every role, status and type.

spec.expr: sum(max by (tailscale_user_role, tailscale_user_status, tailscale_user_type) (last_over_time(tailscale_users_count_ratio[2h]))) or vector(0)

spec.title: Device keys ≤7d
spec.description: Device node keys expiring within 7 days.

spec.title: ACL changed
spec.description: Time since the ACL policy last changed.

spec.title: Flow logging
spec.description: Tailnet network-flow-logging feature state.

spec.title: Exporter up (summary)
spec.description: Whether the exporter process feeding this dashboard is reporting alive. Down means every panel here is stale, not that the tailnet is quiet.

spec.title: Collectors OK (summary)
spec.description: Collectors whose last scrape succeeded. A drop here empties whichever panels that collector feeds; the degradation row below names it.

spec.title: Scrape errors/s (summary)
spec.description: Collector scrape attempts failing per second, fleet-wide. Non-zero opens the degradation-detail row below.

spec.title: Export failures/s
spec.description: OTLP exports failing per second. Data is being collected but not delivered, so panels here go stale while the tailnet is fine.

spec.title: Network throughput
spec.description: Total flow throughput (rollup if present, else raw).

spec.title: Audit & flow events/s
spec.description: Combined tailnet event rate — configuration-audit events and network flows. The audit line is broken down by action and origin in the row below.

spec.title: Devices online over time
spec.description: Online device count against the total the exporter can see — the trend behind the Tailnet health tiles.

spec.title: Audit events/s by action
spec.description: Configuration-audit events per second, split by the action performed.

spec.title: Audit events/s by origin
spec.description: The same audit events split by where they originated (admin console, API, client, ...).

spec.title: Tailnet features
spec.description: Per-feature enabled (1) / disabled (0).

spec.title: Tailnet settings
spec.description: Per-setting enabled (1) / disabled (0) for the tailnet's configuration switches.

spec.title: Scrape errors/s by collector
spec.description: Which collector is failing, and how hard. Whatever panels that collector feeds are the ones reading empty for the wrong reason. Follow "Exporter health →" in the controls menu for the full per-stage diagnosis.

spec.title: Last scrape age by collector
spec.description: Since when: seconds elapsed since each collector last completed a scrape. A row aging past its configured interval is a collector that stopped running rather than one that is erroring. Follow "Exporter health →" in the controls menu for the full per-stage diagnosis.

spec.title: Component errors/s (summary)
spec.description: Which internal stage is erroring when no single collector is — processors, receivers, the checkpoint store. Follow "Exporter health →" in the controls menu for the full per-stage diagnosis.

spec.title: Tailnets observed
spec.description: Number of distinct tailnets observed by this exporter instance (excluding the placeholder '-').

spec.title: Providers
spec.description: Control-plane provider (tailscale, headscale) and its active series count.

spec.title: Tailnet scorecard
spec.description: Per-tailnet health scorecard: online device count, worst scrape staleness, and API error rate.

spec.title: Per-tailnet online devices over time
spec.description: Count of online devices per tailnet over time.

spec.title: Unrestricted ACL rules
spec.description: Total ACL rules that grant unrestricted access (wildcard src/dst). Any non-zero value warrants review.

spec.title: Auto-approved exit nodes
spec.description: ACL auto-approver entries for exit-node routes. Review whether automatic exit-node approval is intended.

spec.title: Unapproved subnet routes
spec.description: Subnet routes advertised but not yet approved by an admin.

defaults.noValue: No subnet-route data — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) and a control plane that reports approved routes.

spec.title: Untagged devices
spec.description: Devices not associated with any ACL tag — harder to audit and apply granular policies to.

defaults.noValue: No device-tag data — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) and a control plane that reports device tags.

spec.title: Pending exit-node shares
spec.description: Pending device share invitations that grant exit-node access.

defaults.noValue: No device-invite data — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices.collect_device_invites).

spec.title: SSH wildcard enabled
spec.description: Whether the tailnet ACL contains a wildcard SSH rule.

spec.title: Online
spec.description: Devices currently reporting as online, within the tab's OS/host/user/tag filters.

spec.title: Total
spec.description: Devices the control plane knows about, online or not, within the tab's filters.

spec.title: Offline
spec.description: Devices registered but not currently connected. Read alongside 'Stale devices (>30d)' below, which separates briefly-offline from abandoned.

spec.title: Updates available
spec.description: Devices whose control plane reports a newer Tailscale client available.

defaults.noValue: No device update data — needs the devices collector and a control plane that reports update availability.

spec.title: Distinct users
spec.description: Users with at least one connected device, counted from the per-user connected gauge rather than inferred from device ownership.

defaults.noValue: No per-user data — needs the users collector and cardinality.per_entity.user.

spec.title: Devices by OS
spec.description: Device count per OS, kept split by authorization and shared-in state — an OS total that sums those away hides the devices an admin still has to act on.

spec.title: Online vs total
spec.description: Online device count against the registered total over time; a widening gap is devices dropping off rather than leaving the tailnet.

spec.title: Devices by OS over time
spec.description: Stacked OS mix over time with authorization and shared-in state preserved, so a growing band of unauthorized or external devices is visible rather than absorbed.

spec.title: Authorized (internal)
spec.description: Devices belonging to this tailnet that an admin has authorized.

defaults.noValue: No device inventory — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) reporting tailscale.devices.count.

spec.title: Unauthorized (internal)
spec.description: Devices registered to this tailnet and waiting on an admin authorization decision. They hold a node key but carry no ACL grants until authorized.

defaults.noValue: No device inventory — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) reporting tailscale.devices.count.

spec.title: External (shared-in)
spec.description: Devices shared in from another tailnet. This tailnet cannot tag them, authorize them or read their version, so fleet-hygiene numbers exclude them.

defaults.noValue: No device inventory — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) reporting tailscale.devices.count.

spec.title: Population split over time
spec.description: The three populations over time. They partition the fleet, so the stack total is the device count and no device is counted in two bands.

spec.title: Device share invite log
spec.description: One INFO line per device-share invite seen during collection — the sharing device, the invitee, the accepting user when accepted, and the delivery state (emailed / manual_link / unknown). Needs collect_device_invites, which costs one API call per device and is off by default; filter with the Log filter variable. The invite URL is a bearer token and is never emitted.

spec.title: Stale devices (>30d)
spec.description: Devices not seen in over 30 days (last-seen staleness) — candidates for decommissioning. Companion to the per-device 'Last seen' table below.

spec.title: Untagged
spec.description: Devices not associated with any ACL tag.

spec.title: Ephemeral
spec.description: Ephemeral devices currently registered.

spec.title: Outdated (≥N behind)
spec.description: Devices running a client version that is at least one minor release behind the fleet latest.

defaults.noValue: No fleet version comparison — enable version_checks.devices (and the upstream latest version must be reachable).

spec.title: Exporter update available
spec.description: Whether a newer version of the tailscale2otel exporter is available.

defaults.noValue: No self update-check data — enable version_checks.self (dev builds never report).

spec.title: Latest stable
spec.description: The latest stable Tailscale client version seen in this fleet.

spec.title: Clients by version
spec.description: Fleet distribution by Tailscale client version.

spec.title: Fleet tags (rollup)
spec.description: Device count per ACL tag across the fleet. Counts individual tags, so a device carrying two tags is counted under each.

spec.title: Device age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: Time since devices joined the tailnet. External/shared-in devices report no creation time and are excluded rather than counted as brand new.

spec.title: Devices by distribution
spec.description: OS distribution mix. Only clients that report a distribution appear (most non-Linux clients do not); beyond 50 pairs the tail folds into __other__.

spec.title: Devices by distribution (per-device)
spec.description: Device count per distribution derived from the PER-DEVICE distro gauge, so it honours the tab's host filter — the roll-up beside it does not and is emitted unconditionally. The two disagreeing means either the host filter is biting or the per-device series are switched off. Codename is carried on the gauge but deliberately not grouped on here; the roll-up splits by it.

defaults.noValue: No per-device distribution series — needs cardinality.per_entity.device and the devices collector (collectors.devices). Only clients that report a distribution are counted at all.

spec.title: Devices by country
spec.description: Devices per country, geolocated from the first globally-routable magicsock endpoint each device advertises. Devices with no globally-routable endpoint, or that the local GeoIP database does not cover, are simply ABSENT — there is no 'unknown' bucket, so the bars will not sum to the fleet total.

defaults.noValue: No device geolocation series — needs enrichment.geoip.enabled and collect_connectivity. Devices with no globally-routable endpoint are absent entirely; there is no 'unknown' bucket to read as zero.

spec.title: Updates available
spec.description: Devices with a client update available.

spec.title: Device key expiry (time until)
spec.description: Time until each device node key expires. Devices with key expiry disabled never appear here — see the 'Device security flags' row on the Posture & Security sub-tab.

spec.title: Last seen (time since)
spec.description: Time since each device was last seen.

spec.title: Device security flags (per device)
spec.description: Per-device security flags. A column is blank when this control plane does not report that field at all, which is not the same as reporting it off.

defaults.noValue: No per-device series — needs cardinality.per_entity.device, and a control plane that reports this field.

spec.title: Most-behind devices (top-N)
spec.description: Devices furthest behind the fleet's latest version (top-N by minor version gap; set the count with the Top N variable).

defaults.noValue: No per-device version-skew series — needs version_checks.devices and cardinality.per_entity.device, and the upstream latest version must be reachable.

spec.title: Tailscale SSH enabled (fleet)
spec.description: Devices accepting Tailscale SSH sessions, from the fleet roll-up (emitted regardless of cardinality.per_entity.device).

defaults.noValue: Not reported — needs a control plane that reports Tailscale SSH state, and the devices collector.

spec.title: Key expiry disabled (fleet)
spec.description: Devices whose node key never expires. These are invisible to every key-expiry panel on this tab, so this is the only place they show up.

defaults.noValue: Not reported — needs a control plane that reports node-key expiry state, and the devices collector.

spec.title: Tailscale SSH enabled (devices)
spec.description: Same count derived from the per-device gauge, so it honours the tab's OS/host/user/tag filters. Diverging from the fleet roll-up means the filters bite.

defaults.noValue: Not reported — needs a control plane that reports Tailscale SSH state, and the devices collector.

spec.title: Key expiry disabled (devices)
spec.description: Per-device view of never-expiring node keys, filterable to a host or tag.

defaults.noValue: Not reported — needs a control plane that reports node-key expiry state, and the devices collector.

spec.title: Blocking incoming connections
spec.description: Devices refusing inbound tailnet connections. Protective, but it also makes a device unreachable for admin access — read it as configuration, not as a fault.

defaults.noValue: No per-device series — needs cardinality.per_entity.device, and a control plane that reports this field.

spec.title: Multiple simultaneous connections
spec.description: Devices whose identity is in use by more than one client at once — a duplicated node key or a cloned state store.

defaults.noValue: No per-device series — needs cardinality.per_entity.device, and a control plane that reports this field.

spec.title: Posture identity disabled
spec.description: Devices exempted from posture-identity collection, so posture-gated ACL rules cannot evaluate them.

defaults.noValue: No per-device series — needs cardinality.per_entity.device, and a control plane that reports this field.

spec.title: Keys already expired
spec.description: Devices whose node key has already expired (per-device expiry gauge; clears after re-auth).

spec.title: Median days-to-expiry
spec.description: Median days until device key expiry across the fleet.

spec.title: Devices by days-to-expiry bucket
spec.description: Current device count per days-to-key-expiry band, from the per-device expiry gauge (point-in-time, non-cumulative; clears after re-auth).

spec.expr: label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) <= 0), "band", "expired", "", "") or label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) > 0 and (max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) < 7*86400), "band", "<=7d", "", "") or label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) >= 7*86400 and (max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) < 30*86400), "band", "7-30d", "", "") or label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) >= 30*86400 and (max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) < 90*86400), "band", "30-90d", "", "") or label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) >= 90*86400 and (max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) < 180*86400), "band", "90-180d", "", "") or label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) >= 180*86400 and (max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) < 365*86400), "band", "180-365d", "", "") or label_replace(count((max by (host_id) (last_over_time(tailscale_device_key_expiry_seconds[2h])) - time()) >= 365*86400), "band", ">365d", "", "")

spec.title: Posture overview
spec.description: Per-device posture: OS, client version, auto-update, encryption, track.

spec.title: Clients by version
spec.description: Device count by reported Tailscale client version, from posture data.

spec.title: Direct-capable %
spec.description: Fraction of devices capable of direct (non-relay) connections.

spec.title: Hard-NAT %
spec.description: Fraction of devices behind hard NAT (require relay for inbound connections).

spec.title: Client capability support
spec.description: Number of devices supporting each connectivity capability.

spec.title: Direct-capable coverage (per-device)
spec.description: Share of reporting devices that look able to hold a direct connection (UDP usable and not behind a hard NAT). An eligibility heuristic, not the path actually in use — cross-check against 'Direct-capable %' beside it.

defaults.noValue: No per-device connectivity series — needs collect_connectivity and cardinality.per_entity.device.

spec.title: IPv6 support coverage
spec.description: Share of reporting devices whose OS supports IPv6. Says nothing about whether IPv6 connectivity is actually available on their network.

defaults.noValue: No per-device connectivity series — needs collect_connectivity and cardinality.per_entity.device.

spec.title: UDP blocked (DERP-forced)
spec.description: Devices whose current network blocks UDP. Every one of their peer connections is relayed through DERP, which costs latency and relay capacity.

defaults.noValue: No per-device connectivity series — needs collect_connectivity and cardinality.per_entity.device.

spec.title: Endpoint candidates per device
spec.description: Magicsock UDP endpoint candidates advertised per device. Few candidates means fewer chances of a direct path; the addresses themselves are never emitted.

defaults.noValue: No per-device connectivity series — needs collect_connectivity and cardinality.per_entity.device.

spec.title: NAT → relay pressure
spec.description: Correlation between hard-NAT fraction and relay endpoint count over time.

spec.title: Connectivity by device
spec.description: Per-device transport situation: direct-path eligibility, UDP usability, IPv6 support and endpoint-candidate count. Click a host to scope the whole dashboard to it.

defaults.noValue: No per-device connectivity series — needs collect_connectivity and cardinality.per_entity.device.

spec.title: Needs relay (hard-NAT)
spec.description: Devices behind hard NAT that require relay for inbound peer connections.

spec.title: Exit nodes advertised
spec.description: Exit nodes currently in the 'advertised' state.

spec.title: Exit nodes enabled
spec.description: Exit nodes currently in the 'enabled' state.

spec.title: Unapproved subnet routes
spec.description: Subnet routes advertised but not yet approved by an admin.

spec.title: Enabled subnet routes
spec.description: Distinct subnet CIDRs approved on at least one device (exit-node default routes excluded). Read against 'Unapproved subnet routes' beside it.

defaults.noValue: No subnet-route data — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) and a control plane that reports approved routes.

spec.title: Advertised subnet routes
spec.description: Distinct subnet CIDRs advertised by at least one device (exit-node default routes excluded). The denominator for the two stats beside it: advertised minus enabled is what is still awaiting approval.

defaults.noValue: No subnet-route data — needs the devices collector (collectors.devices) and a control plane that reports advertised routes.

spec.title: Exit-node inventory
spec.description: Devices currently advertising or acting as exit nodes.

spec.title: Subnet routes — advertised vs enabled
spec.description: Per-device advertised vs enabled subnet-route counts — a gap between the two means an advertised route is still awaiting approval.

spec.title: Subnet-route redundancy by CIDR
spec.description: Number of routers advertising each subnet CIDR (redundancy indicator).

spec.title: DERP latency by host / region
spec.description: Per-device DERP relay latency by region; one row per device/region pair reporting a relay path.

spec.title: Preferred DERP regions
spec.description: Device count per preferred DERP relay region.

spec.title: Throughput (now)
spec.description: Rollup-first: the bounded rollup family is read when present and the raw family only when it is not, so a tailnet running `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode: both` reports each byte once.

spec.title: Packets/s (now)
spec.description: Rollup-first, same fallback as Throughput (now): rollup when present, raw otherwise, never the sum of the two.

spec.title: Flows/s (now)
spec.description: Distinct flow records observed per second, fleet-wide.

spec.title: Flows/s by transport
spec.description: Flow rate split by transport protocol (tcp/udp/other).

spec.title: Flows/s by traffic type
spec.description: Flow rate split by traffic type (virtual/subnet/exit/physical).

spec.title: Reporter trust & consistency
spec.description: One bounded observation per flow record. Trust is configured (node-ID allowlist), tagged (authoritative device tag), untrusted, or unconfigured; consistency compares the verified reporter with the unverified embedded source reference. No raw node ID is present.

spec.title: Observed field omissions
spec.description: Observed missing-field fraction, not inferred Destination Logging state. Privacy-driven destination/port omissions can be expected.

spec.expr: sum by (tailscale_traffic_type, field_class) (rate(tailscale_network_field_observations_total{state="missing"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (tailscale_traffic_type, field_class) (rate(tailscale_network_field_observations_total[$__rate_interval])), 0.000000001)

spec.title: Rejected flow records/s
spec.description: Semantically invalid flow records rejected before any processor side effect, by ingestion source and validation reason. These records are absent from every other panel on this tab, so a sustained rate means the throughput and talker numbers are reading a subset of the feed.

spec.title: Dedup counter conflicts/s
spec.description: Duplicate flow connections whose byte/packet counters disagree with the first observation of the same connection. The first observation stays authoritative, so the conflicting counters are discarded rather than added. Expected while both a poller and a receiver feed the same log type (`collectors.flowlogs.source`); otherwise it is upstream re-delivery.

spec.title: Flow-view store drops/s
spec.description: Flow observations rejected from the local in-memory flow view because their timestamps fall outside its retention or future-skew bounds (`flow_view.*`). OTLP emission is unaffected — these records still reach the metrics and logs on this tab; only the admin flow-view page omits them.

spec.title: Exit-node throughput
spec.description: Bytes relayed through each exit node. Attributed by the reporting node of `traffic_type=exit` flow records and gated by `cardinality.flow.exit_node_attribution` (default on) — independent of the rollup/raw metric mode.

spec.title: Exit-node packets/s
spec.description: Packets relayed through each exit node, same attribution and gating as Exit-node throughput.

spec.title: Observed tailnet bandwidth (flow logs)
spec.description: Bandwidth derived directly from raw flow-log records (Loki), independent of the Prometheus rollup/raw metric mode — a cross-check for the metrics-side throughput panels.

spec.title: Top node-pair talkers (flow logs)
spec.description: Top-N src/dst node pairs by outbound bytes/s, from raw flow-log records.

spec.expr: topk($topn, sum by (tailscale_src_node, tailscale_dst_node) (rate({service_name="tailscale2otel"} | event_name=`tailscale.network.flow` | unwrap tailscale_tx_bytes [$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Throughput by direction
spec.description: Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.title: Throughput by transport
spec.description: Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.title: Throughput by traffic type
spec.description: Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.title: __other__ rollup share
spec.description: Fraction of rollup bytes folded into the bounded __other__ bucket. Raise `cardinality.flow.rollup_top_n` to name more of the traffic.

spec.title: Throughput by path — ROLLUP
spec.description: Rollup bytes split by how the tailnet carried them: `direct` or `derp`. Carried on physical traffic only — the overlay traffic types describe what was carried, not how, so they hold no path at all and are excluded here rather than counted as direct. Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.title: Throughput by DERP region ID — ROLLUP
spec.description: Relayed rollup bytes by the numeric DERP region ID the flow record supplied. NOT joinable with the region NAMES on the device-latency metrics (`tailscale_derp_region`): the API exposes no DERP map to translate between an ID and a name.

spec.title: DERP-relayed share of rollup bytes
spec.description: Share of physical rollup bytes that took a DERP relay rather than a direct path. The flow-side counterpart of Fleet DERP share (now) on the Node Metrics tab, which measures the same thing from tailscaled.

spec.title: Top $topn source nodes
spec.description: Busiest source nodes by rollup byte rate. `__other__` is the bounded remainder bucket, not a node. Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.title: Top $topn destination nodes
spec.description: Busiest destination nodes by rollup byte rate. `__other__` is the bounded remainder bucket, not a node. Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.title: Top destination services
spec.description: Busiest destination services by rollup byte rate; unclassified (empty-service) traffic is excluded so every bar is named. Bounded top-N rollup series, emitted when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `rollup` (the default) or `both`.

spec.expr: topk($topn, sum by (tailscale_dst_service) (rate(tailscale_network_io_rollup_bytes_total{tailscale_tailnet=~"$tailnet", tailscale2otel_provider=~"$provider", network_transport=~"$net_transport", tailscale_traffic_type=~"$traffic_type", tailscale_dst_service!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Unique dst peers per src
spec.description: Distinct destination peers per source node (last flush). Needs `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` `rollup` or `both` AND `cardinality.flow.node_dims`.

spec.title: Unique dst ports per src
spec.description: Distinct destination ports per source node (last flush) — port-level visibility without per-port series. Same prerequisites as the peers table.

spec.title: Throughput by direction (raw)
spec.description: Unbounded per-flow series, emitted only when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `all` or `both`; the row is hidden when the family has no series. Read it instead of the ROLLUP row, never added to it — the rollup is a fold of this same traffic.

spec.title: Packets by direction (raw)
spec.description: Unbounded per-flow series, emitted only when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `all` or `both`; the row is hidden when the family has no series. Read it instead of the ROLLUP row, never added to it — the rollup is a fold of this same traffic.

spec.title: Throughput by transport (raw)
spec.description: Unbounded per-flow series, emitted only when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `all` or `both`; the row is hidden when the family has no series. Read it instead of the ROLLUP row, never added to it — the rollup is a fold of this same traffic.

spec.title: Top $topn source nodes (raw)
spec.description: Busiest source nodes by raw per-flow byte rate — unbounded, so it names every node rather than folding a remainder. Unbounded per-flow series, emitted only when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `all` or `both`; the row is hidden when the family has no series. Read it instead of the ROLLUP row, never added to it — the rollup is a fold of this same traffic.

spec.title: Top $topn destination nodes (raw)
spec.description: Busiest destination nodes by raw per-flow byte rate. Unbounded per-flow series, emitted only when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `all` or `both`; the row is hidden when the family has no series. Read it instead of the ROLLUP row, never added to it — the rollup is a fold of this same traffic.

spec.title: Top $topn destination services (raw)
spec.description: Busiest destination services by raw per-flow byte rate. Unbounded per-flow series, emitted only when `cardinality.flow.metrics_mode` is `all` or `both`; the row is hidden when the family has no series. Read it instead of the ROLLUP row, never added to it — the rollup is a fold of this same traffic.

spec.expr: topk($topn, sum by (tailscale_dst_service) (rate(tailscale_network_io_bytes_total{tailscale_tailnet=~"$tailnet", tailscale2otel_provider=~"$provider", network_transport=~"$net_transport", tailscale_traffic_type=~"$traffic_type", tailscale_dst_service!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Flow log stream
spec.description: Raw flow-log lines as received, newest first; narrow them with the Log filter control. This is the unaggregated record behind the rollup and raw panels above.

spec.title: Targets up
spec.description: Node-metrics scrape targets currently reachable. Zero here with a healthy Discovery OK means targets were found and none answered — the panels below are empty because of the targets, not because of the tailnet. Per-target detail is on the Exporter health dashboard's Collection tab.

spec.title: Discovery OK
spec.description: Whether the last node-metrics target-discovery pass succeeded. A failure here explains an empty tab on its own: nothing was scraped because nothing was found. Discovery detail is on the Exporter health dashboard's Collection tab.

spec.title: Inbound bytes/s
spec.description: Raw tailscaled inbound byte rate, per node.

spec.title: Outbound bytes/s
spec.description: Raw tailscaled outbound byte rate, per node.

spec.title: Inbound packets/s
spec.description: Raw tailscaled inbound packet rate, per node.

spec.title: Outbound packets/s
spec.description: Raw tailscaled outbound packet rate, per node.

spec.title: Outbound dropped packets/s by node
spec.description: Outbound packets dropped by tailscaled per node, with the raw upstream `reason` label. `acl` here is the packet filter enforcing policy, not a fault — the curated row below separates the two. Needs the node-metrics scraper (`node_metrics.enabled`) against a tailscaled exposing `tailscaled_outbound_dropped_packets_total`.

spec.title: Advertised routes
spec.description: Per-node count of subnet routes advertised, from raw tailscaled state.

spec.title: Approved routes
spec.description: Per-node count of subnet routes approved, from raw tailscaled state.

spec.title: Health messages
spec.description: tailscaled self-reported health warnings.

spec.title: Home DERP region
spec.description: Each node's current home DERP region ID, from raw tailscaled state.

spec.title: Peer relay endpoints
spec.description: Per-node count of peer-relay endpoints, from raw tailscaled state.

spec.title: % traffic via DERP relay by node
spec.description: Fraction of each node's traffic relayed via DERP rather than sent direct. Sustained high values indicate NAT-traversal problems (added latency).

spec.expr: sum by (tailscale_node) (label_replace(rate(tailscaled_inbound_bytes_total{path="derp"}[$__rate_interval]), "dir", "in", "", "") or label_replace(rate(tailscaled_outbound_bytes_total{path="derp"}[$__rate_interval]), "dir", "out", "", "")) / clamp_min(sum by (tailscale_node) (label_replace(rate(tailscaled_inbound_bytes_total[$__rate_interval]), "dir", "in", "", "") or label_replace(rate(tailscaled_outbound_bytes_total[$__rate_interval]), "dir", "out", "", "")), 1)

spec.title: Throughput by path
spec.description: Total tailnet throughput split by path: DERP relay vs direct IPv4 vs direct IPv6.

spec.title: Fleet DERP share (now)
spec.description: Fleet-wide fraction of bytes relayed via DERP.

spec.title: Path mix (DERP / IPv4 / IPv6)
spec.description: Current total throughput split by raw tailscaled path (DERP/IPv4/IPv6).

spec.title: Best latency per DERP region
spec.description: Best (minimum) device→DERP-region latency across the tailnet, per region.

spec.title: Devices per DERP region
spec.description: Number of devices reporting latency to each DERP region.

spec.title: Preferred DERP region distribution
spec.description: Number of devices that prefer each DERP region.

spec.title: Active health warnings by type
spec.description: Active tailscaled client health-warning messages across the fleet, by health type (curated tailscale.node.health_messages; alert ts2o-node-health-warnings).

spec.title: Traffic mix by path (direct / DERP / peer-relay)
spec.description: Tailnet data-plane throughput split by curated path bucket: direct, DERP relay, or peer relay (curated tailscale.node.io — includes the peer_relay bucket the raw tailscaled path label does not separate).

spec.title: Packets/s by path (curated)
spec.description: Data-plane PACKET rate by curated path bucket — the packet counterpart of Traffic mix by path. Read alongside it: a path whose packet share far exceeds its byte share is carrying small frames (keepalives, handshake churn) rather than useful payload, which the byte panel alone hides.

spec.title: Path mix (now)
spec.description: Current data-plane byte rate by curated path bucket (direct / DERP / peer-relay).

spec.title: Home DERP region (curated)
spec.description: Each node's current home DERP region, carried as the region ID in the value column. The `_ratio` suffix is the OTLP unit-`1` gauge naming rule, not a fraction — read the number as an ID. It is NOT joinable with the region NAMES on the DERP-region rollup panels below; the API exposes no DERP map to translate between an ID and a name.

spec.title: Policy drops (ACL)
spec.description: Packets the tailscaled packet filter dropped because the tailnet policy does not permit them. This is the ACL working, NOT a fault, so the panel carries no error colouring and nothing here should be escalated on its own. A step change is worth correlating with an ACL edit (Security & Audit tab); a sustained level is normal. Error-class drops are the panel beside this one.

spec.title: Error & malformed drops by reason
spec.description: Every documented drop reason EXCEPT `acl`. `error` is the one to escalate; `too_short` / `fragment` / `unknown_protocol` point at a malformed or misrouted sender; `multicast` / `link_local_unicast` are traffic the tailnet does not carry and are usually a chatty LAN rather than a fault; `other` is a reason this build does not recognize yet, so a rising `other` means the upstream vocabulary moved. Sustained `error`/`unknown_protocol`/`other` is the escalation signal, not a single spike.

spec.title: Drop share by reason
spec.description: Each reason's share of all offered packets (delivered + dropped), so a drop rate can be read against traffic volume instead of in isolation. Deliberately unthresholded and including `acl`: the ratio is context, and a high but steady ACL share is a strict policy, not an incident.

spec.title: Peer-relay throughput by node
spec.description: Bytes each node forwarded while acting as a peer relay (curated tailscale.node.peer_relay.io).

spec.title: Peer-relay throughput by transport
spec.description: Relayed bytes by ingress and egress transport. A heavy udp4 -> udp6 (or reverse) share means the relay is bridging address families rather than just forwarding.

spec.title: Peer-relay packets/s by transport
spec.description: Relayed PACKET rate by the same transport transition. Held against the byte panel it gives the mean relayed frame size: packets climbing while bytes hold flat is a relay carrying overhead rather than payload.

spec.title: Peer-relay endpoints by state
spec.description: Peer-relay endpoints split by connection state. A persistently high `connecting` count against a low `open` count is a relay failing to establish sessions.

spec.title: Peer-relay endpoint share by state
spec.description: The same endpoint states as a share of all peer-relay endpoints, so a fleet that grows does not look like a relay regression. Sustained non-`open` share is the shape to alert on; a transient `connecting` spike after a restart is not.

spec.title: Security/lifecycle changes/s
spec.description: Rate of audit change events by change kind and action.

spec.title: Device churn
spec.description: Device add/remove/update rate over time.

spec.title: Changes by actor type
spec.description: Total change events in the selected range, broken out by actor type (user/api-key/etc).

spec.title: Audit actions over time
spec.description: Config-audit events over time, by action (create/update/delete/...).

spec.title: Audit events (range)
spec.description: Total config-audit events over the selected dashboard time range.

spec.title: Failed changes — WARN (range)
spec.description: Audit events emitted at WARN (the event carried an error).

spec.title: Audit events by target type
spec.description: Config-audit events over time, by the kind of object changed.

spec.title: Audit action breakdown (logs)
spec.description: Audit log action/target-type breakdown — no actor identity, safe to show when PII redaction is active.

spec.title: Top $topn actors over time
spec.description: Top-N config-change actors by event count. Hidden on explicit PII redaction of actor identity.

spec.title: Top $topn targets over time
spec.description: Top-N config-change targets by event count. Hidden on explicit PII redaction of actor identity.

spec.title: Audit: metric vs log
spec.description: Metric change counters vs Loki log event rate — divergence indicates missing ingestion path.

spec.title: Recent configuration changes
spec.description: Live audit stream; filter with the Log filter variable.

spec.title: Log stream — $log_event
spec.description: Pick an event type with the Log event variable; filter with Log filter.

spec.title: Log volume by event
spec.description: Volume of every exporter log event by event_name — the denominator for the stream beside it, and the fastest way to see a signal stop being emitted.

spec.title: Wildcard rules
spec.description: Number of ACL rules containing wildcards, by section and position.

spec.title: Unrestricted rules (grants)
spec.description: Grant rules with no destination restriction.

spec.title: Unrestricted rules (acls)
spec.description: ACL rules with no destination restriction.

spec.title: SSH wildcard
spec.description: Whether any SSH rule uses a wildcard source or destination.

spec.title: Auto-approvers by kind
spec.description: Count of auto-approver entries by kind (routes/exit-nodes).

spec.title: Posture-gated rules
spec.description: Rules that require a passing device-posture check, by section.

spec.title: Unrestricted ACL/grant rules (log detail)
spec.description: One WARN record per unrestricted rule — wildcard `src` AND wildcard `dst` in a non-deny rule — naming the policy section (tailscale_acl_section) and the offending src/dst entries (tailscale_acl_rule). This is the detail behind the 'Unrestricted rules' counts above: the counts say how many, this says which. Needs the acl collector (collectors.acl); the rule text is free-text and is dropped when pii_filter.free_text_details is on, leaving the section only.

spec.title: Tailnet-lock errors
spec.description: Devices with a non-empty tailnet-lock error (e.g. an unsigned node). >0 means a signing node must sign the affected keys.

spec.title: Nodes with tailnet-lock errors
spec.description: Per-device tailnet-lock error events; the error text is the log body.

spec.title: Integrations configured
spec.description: Configured device-posture (MDM/EDR) integrations, e.g. Intune.

spec.title: Devices matched by integration
spec.description: Devices matched to a provider host by each posture integration.

spec.title: Oldest sync age
spec.description: Time since the least-recently-synced integration last synced (alert on staleness).

defaults.noValue: No posture integration has reported a sync yet.

spec.title: Posture match rate
spec.description: Fraction of possible-match devices that were actually matched by the integration.

spec.title: Integration sync detail
spec.description: Per integration: matched / possible-match / provider-host counts and sync age.

spec.title: Encryption coverage
spec.description: Average encryption coverage across devices (Intune isEncrypted attribute).

spec.title: Compliance distribution
spec.description: Distribution of attribute values for the selected posture attribute.

spec.title: Devices failing posture attr
spec.description: Devices with a failing (0) posture attribute. Hidden when host-name redaction is active.

spec.title: Posture attribute expiry — time remaining
spec.description: Time left on each posture attribute that carries an explicit expiry, per device and attribute. A negative value has already lapsed. Only attributes explicitly set WITH an expiry appear at all — most never carry one, so an empty panel is normal rather than a fault. Gated by collect_posture and the attribute_namespaces allow-list.

defaults.noValue: No posture-attribute expiry series. Only attributes explicitly set WITH an expiry appear here — most posture attributes never carry one, so an empty panel is the normal reading, not a fault. Needs the devices collector with collect_posture, and the attribute inside the attribute_namespaces allow-list.

spec.title: Expiring posture attributes (log detail)
spec.description: One WARN record per device+attribute whose posture-attribute expiry falls inside the fixed 14-day warn window and has not yet lapsed. Carries host_name, host_id, the attribute key and tailscale_device_attribute_expires_in_days. Needs the devices collector with collect_posture; hidden when host-name redaction is active.

spec.title: Auto-update coverage
spec.description: Fraction of devices with Tailscale client auto-update enabled.

spec.title: State-encryption coverage
spec.description: Fraction of devices reporting an encrypted local state store.

spec.title: Devices needing update
spec.description: Count of devices with a client update available.

defaults.noValue: No device update data — needs the devices collector and a control plane that reports update availability.

spec.title: Release track split
spec.description: Device count by Tailscale release track (stable/unstable), from posture data.

spec.title: Client version distribution
spec.description: Device count by reported Tailscale client version, from posture data.

spec.title: Device posture snapshot
spec.description: Per-device posture log stream (host identity in body — hidden when host-name redaction is active). Filter with the Log filter variable.

spec.title: Device keys ≤7d
spec.description: Devices whose node key expires within 7 days and has not already expired. Each one drops off the tailnet when it lapses unless it is re-authed or marked as never-expiring.

spec.title: Device keys ≤30d
spec.description: Devices whose node key expires within 30 days — the early-warning counterpart to the 7-day tile, sized for a rotation window rather than an incident.

spec.title: API/auth keys ≤7d
spec.description: Tailnet API keys and auth keys expiring within 7 days. An expiring API key takes whatever automation holds it down with it — including this exporter.

spec.title: API/auth keys ≤30d
spec.description: Tailnet API keys and auth keys expiring within 30 days.

spec.title: Expiring device keys (log detail)
spec.description: One WARN record per device whose node key expires inside the fixed 14-day warn window and has not yet lapsed. Carries host_name, host_id and tailscale_device_key_expires_in_days — the actionable per-device detail the fleet-wide key-expiry histogram cannot give you. Needs the devices collector; hidden when host-name redaction is active.

spec.title: Expiring auth keys & credentials (log detail)
spec.description: One WARN record per auth key or OAuth credential expiring inside the configured `expiry_warn` window. Carries the key id, type, auth kind, owner, tags and tailscale_key_expires_in_seconds — seconds REMAINING, not an absolute timestamp, so it counts down rather than up. Needs the keys collector. Read it against the expiry tiles above: those say how many, this says which.

spec.title: Key age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: How old the tailnet's credentials are. A rising p90 means long-lived keys nobody is rotating, which expiry panels alone cannot show.

defaults.noValue: No key age data — needs the keys collector (collectors.keys). Keys whose creation time the API omits are skipped.

spec.title: Keys by owner and type
spec.description: Who holds the tailnet's credentials, by owning user id and key type. Concentration on one owner is a departure risk; the owner is an opaque user id, not an email.

defaults.noValue: No key ownership data — needs the keys collector (collectors.keys). Keys with no owning user are excluded.

spec.title: Unrestricted OAuth clients
spec.description: OAuth clients whose device-create capability is restricted to no tags at all, so any device they register can claim any tag.

defaults.noValue: No per-credential key series — needs the keys collector (collectors.keys) and cardinality.per_entity.key.

spec.title: OAuth client tag restrictions
spec.description: Allowed-tag COUNT per OAuth client credential (0 is unrestricted). Distinct from the tag-restriction CLASS panel below and from tailscale.key.tags, the tags a credential auto-applies to devices it creates.

defaults.noValue: No per-credential key series — needs the keys collector (collectors.keys) and cardinality.per_entity.key.

spec.title: Credential privilege class (blast radius)
spec.description: The API privilege class each credential actually holds, ranked by blast radius: none < read < all_read < write < all. `all` is unrestricted read AND write, including API surfaces that do not exist yet — a credential that can do anything Tailscale later adds. The gauge is zero-seeded across every class per credential, so this panel filters to == 1 to show the one class that is set.

defaults.noValue: No per-credential key series — needs the keys collector (collectors.keys) and cardinality.per_entity.key.

spec.title: OAuth client tag restriction class
spec.description: Whether each OAuth client carries a tag restriction of its own: `none` or `restricted`. READ THE POLARITY — `none` means NO restriction, so the credential may create devices carrying ANY tag; it is the BROAD case, not the narrow one. Only OAuth clients carry this field. Zero-seeded across both classes, so this panel filters to == 1.

defaults.noValue: No per-credential key series — needs the keys collector (collectors.keys) and cardinality.per_entity.key.

spec.title: User account age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: Age of the tailnet's user accounts. Users with no creation time are omitted rather than reported as age zero.

defaults.noValue: No user age data — needs the users collector (collectors.users). Users with no reported creation time are skipped.

spec.title: Pending user-invite age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: Time since Tailscale last emailed each unaccepted user invite. Manual-link invites carry no delivery timestamp and are omitted.

defaults.noValue: No pending user-invite age data — needs the users collector (collectors.users) and at least one emailed invite.

spec.title: Pending device-invite age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: How long unaccepted device shares have been outstanding. A long tail is a standing offer of access nobody took up and nobody revoked.

defaults.noValue: No pending device-invite age data — needs collect_device_invites. Accepted invites are excluded.

spec.title: Contact needs verification
spec.description: Whether any tailnet contact address requires re-verification (admin/security/billing).

defaults.noValue: No contact data — enable the contacts collector (collectors.contacts).

spec.title: Device shares: pending vs accepted
spec.description: Device share invites grouped by accepted status. A pending invite is an outstanding grant nobody has taken up yet; it stays live until it is revoked, so a growing pending count is unretired access, not a backlog.

spec.title: Exit-node-granting shares
spec.description: Device share invites that also grant exit-node use, so the recipient can route their traffic through the shared device. Review whether that is intended — it is a broader grant than sharing the device itself.

spec.title: Multi-use shares
spec.description: Device share invites that can be redeemed more than once, so a single leaked link admits an unbounded number of recipients.

spec.title: ACL last changed
spec.description: Time since the tailnet policy file was last modified. A policy that has not moved in months is normal; this is here to date a change you are already investigating, not as a health signal.

spec.title: ACL size
spec.description: Serialized size of the active policy file. Useful as a change detector alongside ACL last changed — a large jump is a rewrite, not an edit.

spec.title: ACL rules by section
spec.description: Rule count per top-level policy section (acls, grants, ssh, nodeAttrs, tagOwners, ...). Structure of the policy, not a verdict on it.

spec.title: Auto-approvers (inventory)
spec.description: Auto-approver entries by kind (routes / exit node). Inventory only — whether an auto-approver is too permissive is a Security & Audit question.

spec.title: Posture-gated rules (inventory)
spec.description: Rules carrying a device-posture condition, by section. Counts how much of the policy depends on posture data actually arriving.

spec.title: ACL policy validated
spec.description: 1 when the active policy — including the tests embedded in its own `tests` section — validated cleanly on the last check. Empty rather than 0 when the validate call is unavailable; tailscale2otel.api.availability carries that state separately.

defaults.noValue: No validation result. Prerequisites: collectors.acl.enabled with collectors.acl.validate, and a credential carrying the policy_file:read scope. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Validation issues (last check)
spec.description: Counts from the last policy validation. Errors and test failures are reported separately by the API, so errors stays 0 in the common case while an embedded test fails. Warnings include advisory findings such as a group that is not syncing from SCIM.

spec.title: Validation issues by kind (logs)
spec.description: One WARN per non-zero issue kind (error / warning / test_failure) per check. The validator's free-text messages carry rule text, user names and addresses and are deliberately never emitted, so the kind is all there is here — read the policy itself for the detail.

spec.title: MagicDNS
spec.description: Whether MagicDNS is turned on for the tailnet. With it off, devices resolve each other by address only and every search-path and split-DNS setting below has no effect.

spec.title: Nameservers
spec.description: Global nameservers configured for the tailnet. Zero means devices keep their local resolvers.

spec.title: Search paths
spec.description: Search domains appended to unqualified names on every device. Each one adds a resolution attempt, so a long list slows first-lookup latency.

spec.title: Split-DNS zones
spec.description: Zones routed to a specific resolver rather than the global nameservers. The per-zone resolver addresses are in the Resolvers table below.

spec.title: Override local DNS
spec.description: Whether the tailnet's nameservers replace each device's local resolvers outright, rather than being added alongside them.

spec.title: Exit-node resolvers
spec.description: Configured resolvers marked usable while a device is routing through an exit node.

spec.title: Search domains
spec.description: The individual search domains behind the Search paths count, one bar each — the fastest way to spot a stale or duplicated entry.

spec.title: Resolvers
spec.description: DNS resolver configuration: each resolver's address, kind (global or split-DNS) and whether it stays in use behind an exit node. FIX-3: no domain label on the live wire, so a split-DNS resolver is identified by address rather than by the zone it serves.

defaults.noValue: No resolver series. Prerequisites: collectors.dns.enabled and a tailnet with at least one global or split-DNS resolver configured. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Tailnet settings
spec.description: Per-setting enabled (1) / disabled (0).

spec.title: Device key duration
spec.description: How long a device key stays valid before the device must re-authenticate. The tailnet-wide default; individual devices may have key expiry turned off, which the Fleet view reports.

spec.title: Tailnet features
spec.description: Per-feature enabled (1) / disabled (0).

spec.title: External-tailnets role
spec.description: Role granted to users joining from external tailnets. Values: none / member / admin. Live: role=none.

spec.title: Webhook endpoints
spec.description: Configured webhook endpoints on the tailnet. The Integrations sub-tab breaks the same population down by subscribed event category and by endpoint.

defaults.noValue: No webhook data — needs the webhooks collector and a credential scoped to read webhooks.

spec.title: Stale users (>30d)
spec.description: Users not seen in over 30 days (last-seen staleness). Empty, not zero, when per-user metrics are unavailable; see the Per-user detail row.

defaults.noValue: No per-user data — needs the users collector and cardinality.per_entity.user.

spec.title: User invites
spec.description: Outstanding open user invites, by role and delivery method.

defaults.noValue: No user-invite series. Prerequisites: collectors.users.enabled and a credential that can read tailnet users. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Users by role
spec.description: Tailnet users by assigned role (owner / admin / member / ...). An aggregate of the bounded users.count gauge, so it stays populated with per-user series switched off.

spec.title: Users by status
spec.description: Tailnet users by account status (active / idle / suspended / needs-approval). Suspended and needs-approval accounts still hold a tailnet identity.

spec.title: Users by type
spec.description: Tailnet users by type — a member of the tailnet versus a shared-in user from another tailnet.

spec.title: Per-user detail
spec.description: Per-user connected / device count / time since last seen.

spec.title: Keys by type
spec.description: API and auth keys the tailnet holds, split by key type and by auth kind (user-owned versus OAuth-minted). An aggregate, so it survives cardinality.per_entity.key being switched off.

spec.title: Credential scopes (top-N)
spec.description: Top-N keys by how many scopes they carry — the configuration view of scope sprawl. Excludes the raw key ID; whether a given breadth is too much for its purpose is a Security & Audit question.

defaults.noValue: No per-key scope series. Prerequisites: collectors.keys.enabled and cardinality.per_entity.key. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Key scope inventory (logs)
spec.description: Credential scope values observed in key.scopes log events over the dashboard time range. Counts observations, not keys: one key re-logged each collection tick contributes many.

spec.title: Key expiry (time until)
spec.description: Time until each API/auth key expires.

spec.title: Preauthorized auth keys
spec.description: Count of auth keys marked preauthorized (auto-approved, no manual login).

defaults.noValue: No per-key data — needs the keys collector and cardinality.per_entity.key.

spec.title: OAuth applications
spec.description: Registered OAuth applications on the tailnet. Configuration reference: [collectors.oauth_apps](https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/).

defaults.noValue: No OAuth-application data. Prerequisites: collectors.oauth_apps.enabled, a credential that can read OAuth applications, and a tailnet where the alpha OAuth-apps API is available. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: OAuth apps by privilege class
spec.description: Applications per privilege class, ranked by internal/tsscope: none < read < all_read < write < all. The gauge is zero-seeded across every class, so this counts only the class each app currently holds.

spec.title: OAuth app age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: Fleet age distribution of OAuth applications since their created timestamp. A single bounded histogram, not a per-app series — apps with no created timestamp are omitted rather than recorded as age 0.

spec.title: OAuth app scope & attribute counts
spec.description: Scope sprawl per application: granted scopes, custom node attributes it may set, and how many redirect targets it has configured. All three are counts — the exporter emits no redirect target values and no client credential, so none can be shown here.

spec.title: OAuth application inventory (logs)
spec.description: Granted scope sets observed on the oauth_app.info inventory log, over the dashboard time range. Counts observations, not applications: one app re-logged each collection tick contributes many.

spec.title: Services (VIP)
spec.description: Tailscale Services (VIP services) advertised in the tailnet.

spec.title: Backing hosts by service
spec.description: Backing-host count per Service, bucketed by approval + configured state. Gated by collect_hosts + cardinality.per_entity.service.

spec.title: Port rules per service
spec.description: Port rules exposed by each Service. Gated by cardinality.per_entity.service.

spec.title: VIP service health
spec.description: Merged view: hosts + port-rule count per VIP service. Services with 1 host have no HA. Requires collect_hosts + per_entity.service.

spec.title: Desired-event coverage
spec.description: 1 when a category listed in collectors.webhooks.desired_events has at least one subscribed endpoint. Emitted only for recognised desired categories — a misspelled entry is counted by Unrecognized desired events instead of reading as permanently uncovered.

defaults.noValue: No desired-event expectation. Prerequisites: collectors.webhooks.enabled and a non-empty collectors.webhooks.desired_events list. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Unrecognized desired events
spec.description: Entries in collectors.webhooks.desired_events that are not documented subscription categories — almost always a typo. The offending strings ride the webhook_endpoints.event_mismatch log event, never a metric label, so the count is what a panel can show.

spec.title: Subscribers per event category
spec.description: Endpoints subscribed to each documented category. The full 18-value vocabulary is zero-seeded every tick (plus `other`), so a category nobody listens for reads as an explicit 0 rather than a missing bar.

spec.title: Per-endpoint subscriptions
spec.description: How many categories each endpoint subscribes to, by endpoint id and provider. The destination address, its signing credential and its creator are never emitted, so this identifies an endpoint only by its id.

defaults.noValue: No per-endpoint data. Prerequisites: collectors.webhooks.enabled and cardinality.per_entity.webhook. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Webhook endpoint age (p50 / p90)
spec.description: Age distribution of configured endpoints. Fleet-level with no per-endpoint attributes; an endpoint with no creation timestamp is omitted rather than recorded as age 0, and nothing is emitted when none reports one.

spec.title: Desired-event mismatches (logs)
spec.description: One WARN per desired category that is uncovered or unrecognized. The body names which of the two; the category label is bounded, reading `other` for an unrecognized entry.

spec.title: GeoIP database age since build
spec.description: How old the LOADED database's build is, per database (country / asn). This is MaxMind's build date, not when the file was fetched, which is exactly why it is the right staleness signal: an updater that has silently stopped still leaves a recent file mtime, but the build date keeps aging. Charted as age rather than the raw epoch so it matches the alert, `time() - tailscale_geoip_database_build_time_seconds > 14 * 86400` — the red band here IS that threshold. A database that is not loaded is absent, not stale.

defaults.noValue: No GeoIP series. Prerequisites: enrichment.geoip.enabled with a country or ASN database on disk, and self_observability.enabled. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: GeoIP database downloads
spec.description: MaxMind downloads by edition and result. A panel that is almost entirely `unmodified` is the GOOD state, not a stalled one: each check is conditional and a 304 means the local build is already current, which is what keeps a daily updater inside MaxMind's download quota. `updated` means a newer build was fetched, SHA-256 verified and installed; `failure` means neither happened and the previous database keeps serving.

defaults.noValue: No GeoIP download series. Prerequisites: enrichment.geoip.download.enabled with MaxMind credentials, and self_observability.enabled. Databases supplied by an external geoipupdate cron never produce these. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: GeoIP lookups by database and result
spec.description: Enrichment lookups by database (country / asn / skipped) and result. A high `skipped` share is NORMAL on a tailnet and is not a fault: those are addresses that never reached a database at all, having been rejected as not globally routable — loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, and in particular the Tailscale CGNAT range and ULA, which are never geolocated. `hit` found a record; `miss` means the loaded database has none for that address.

defaults.noValue: No GeoIP series. Prerequisites: enrichment.geoip.enabled with a country or ASN database on disk, and self_observability.enabled. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: GeoIP database reloads
spec.description: Hot-swaps of a database file that changed on disk, by database and result. `success` means the new file was read and swapped in atomically. A `failure` is degraded-but-working rather than an outage: the previously loaded database keeps serving lookups, so pair it with the age panel to see whether enrichment is quietly running on a frozen copy. An unchanged file is not counted at all, so a flat zero line is the steady state.

defaults.noValue: No GeoIP series. Prerequisites: enrichment.geoip.enabled with a country or ASN database on disk, and self_observability.enabled. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Posture integration last-sync errors
spec.description: 1 when an MDM/EDR posture integration's last sync reported an error, per provider and integration. This is the ONLY failure signal these integrations have: `lastSync` advances on every ATTEMPT, successful or not, so the age column beside it goes stale only when syncing stops entirely and stays perfectly fresh through an integration that fails every single run. The raw error text is deliberately never emitted as a label, so read the provider's own console for what actually broke. Age is repeated here from the Security & Audit staleness view so both halves of the pair are on one row.

defaults.noValue: No posture-integration series. Prerequisites: collectors.posture_integrations.enabled and a credential that can read device-posture integrations. See https://m7kni.io/tailscale2otel/configuration/

spec.title: Kubernetes API requests/s
spec.description: Kubernetes API requests proxied through Tailscale, per second. Counts attempts only — the source record carries no response status, so this is request volume, not success or failure rate.

spec.title: Requests by verb
spec.description: Proxied Kubernetes API requests over time, by HTTP verb (get/list/watch/create/update/patch/delete/...). A verb mix shift is worth correlating with a client or access change.

spec.title: Requests by namespace
spec.description: Request rate by target namespace. A cluster-scoped request (no namespace) reports an empty namespace label.

spec.title: Requests by resource (top $topn)
spec.description: Top-N Kubernetes resource types by request count over the selected range. `other` means the resource kind fell outside the bounded admit-set.

spec.title: Requests by user agent (top $topn)
spec.description: Top-N requesting clients by user agent string over the selected range. Not identity — the same person can appear under several agents (kubectl, a controller, a CI job).

spec.title: Sensitive reads/s by resource
spec.description: Read (get/list/watch) attempts against sensitive resource kinds — secrets, service accounts, RBAC objects, token/CSR reviews. Attempts only; RBAC may have refused any of these.

spec.title: Sensitive reads by namespace
spec.description: Sensitive-resource read attempts by target namespace.

spec.title: Sensitive reads by user agent (top $topn)
spec.description: Top-N clients, by user agent, attempting sensitive-resource reads over the selected range.

spec.title: Users reading sensitive resources ($topn)
spec.description: Top-N identities attempting sensitive-resource reads over the selected range. Hidden when email/identity redaction is active.

spec.title: Exec sessions/s by command class
spec.description: Exec/attach/portforward requests against a pod, per second, by the bounded command classification (interactive_shell, recon, credential_read, package_mgmt, net_tool, file_transfer, none, other). Stays visible even when raw command text is redacted.

spec.title: Exec sessions by namespace
spec.description: Exec/attach/portforward request rate by target namespace.

spec.title: Exec sessions by session type
spec.description: Exec/attach/portforward request count over the selected range, by session type.

spec.title: Users by exec/attach/portforward sessions ($topn)
spec.description: Top-N identities requesting exec/attach/portforward sessions over the selected range. Hidden when email/identity redaction is active.

spec.title: Mutations/s by verb
spec.description: Mutating (create/update/patch/delete/deletecollection) request attempts, per second, by verb. Counts the request being made, not that the change was admitted or persisted.

spec.title: Mutations by resource (top $topn)
spec.description: Top-N resource kinds targeted by mutating requests over the selected range.

spec.title: Mutations by namespace
spec.description: Mutating request attempt rate by target namespace.

spec.title: Users making mutating requests ($topn)
spec.description: Top-N identities attempting mutating requests over the selected range. Hidden when email/identity redaction is active.

spec.title: RBAC probes/s by resource
spec.description: SelfSubjectAccessReview/SelfSubjectRulesReview/SubjectAccessReview/TokenReview requests — a client asking what it or another identity is allowed to do — per second. A burst from an unexpected client is the signal; normal for UI clients, which is why no alert ships by default.

spec.title: RBAC probes by namespace
spec.description: Permission-enumeration probe rate by namespace.

spec.title: Users making RBAC/permission probes ($topn)
spec.description: Top-N identities making permission-enumeration probes over the selected range. Hidden when email/identity redaction is active.

spec.title: Sessions started/s by type
spec.description: Recorded terminal sessions started against a Kubernetes pod, per second, by session type. Session completeness cannot be observed, so this counts starts only.

spec.title: Sessions by namespace
spec.description: Recorded terminal-session start rate by target namespace.

spec.title: Sessions by command class
spec.description: Recorded terminal-session starts over the selected range, by the bounded launch-command classification. Stays visible even when raw command text is redacted.

spec.title: Users starting terminal sessions ($topn)
spec.description: Top-N identities starting recorded terminal sessions over the selected range. Hidden when email/identity redaction is active.

spec.title: Schema drift events/s by field
spec.description: Kubernetes-audit schema vocabulary observations, per second, by field and whether the value is known to this collector version. A healthy feed reports nothing here — any nonzero rate means an unexpected event type or enum value, worth checking after an operator/recorder upgrade.

spec.title: Schema drift events (range)
spec.description: Total schema-drift observations over the selected range. A healthy feed reports 0; any nonzero count means upstream's unversioned event schema moved.

spec.title: Recent Kubernetes API requests
spec.description: Live stream of proxied Kubernetes API requests; filter with the Log filter variable. Hidden when email or exec-command redaction is active — the record carries requesting identity and, for exec-shaped requests, the raw command.

spec.title: Recent terminal sessions
spec.description: Live stream of recorded terminal-session starts; filter with the Log filter variable. Hidden when email or exec-command redaction is active — the record carries requesting identity and the raw launch command.

spec.title: Secret & sensitive resource reads
spec.description: Who attempted to read secrets, and from where. Attempts only — RBAC may have refused any of these. Hidden under email redaction.

spec.title: Permission enumeration probes
spec.description: Detail behind the RBAC-probe metrics. A burst from an unexpected user agent is the signal; normal for UI clients. Hidden under email redaction.

spec.title: Reads of the recorder's own logs (anti-forensics)
spec.description: Requests to read the tsrecorder's own log objects — a client reaching for the audit trail itself is an anti-forensics indicator. Hidden under email redaction.

spec.title: Exec / attach / port-forward requests
spec.description: Every exec/attach/port-forward request, with the bounded command classification alongside the raw command line when it is not redacted. This is the one investigation panel that can surface command text, so it is the one hidden under exec-command redaction.
